grants.title: GO8606: Remote Training Hubs Network: Central Australia Remote Training Hubs Grant - Round 3
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations via a closed, non-competitive process to apply to deliver services under Program 2.1: Building Skills and Capability from February 2027 to 30 June 2028. The Central Australia Remote Training Hubs Grant, funded through the Remote Training Hubs Network measure, was announced by the Prime Minister on 13 February 2024, under the A Better, Safer Future for Central Australia (Central Australia Plan), to support the delivery of vocational education and training in up to 7 remote community clusters in Central Australia, through the provision of funding for capital assets or improvements, remote training hub coordination and mentoring and participant transport to 30 June 2028. This third round of the Central Australia Remote Training Hubs grant opportunity is open to The Plenty cluster only. The remaining community clusters will be invited to apply in subsequent grant round(s). The Central Australia Mobile Training Units (MTUs) Grant (ID GO7445) is linked to this grant opportunity. If successful, you will be required to work in partnership with the Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) delivering services via the MTUs.

grants.title: GO8341: Modernised Multicultural Grants Program: Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities
grants.summary: Information session An online information session scheduled to be held on Wednesday 7 October 2026 for Batch 2 applicants has been postponed. In the meantime, you can view the recording of an information session held earlier this year for this grant opportunity by visiting Infrastructure for Multicultural Grant – 6 May 2026 Information Session - Meeting Recording. Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for each batch: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 18 May 2026 - ID 2025-5201 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 12 November 2026 - ID 2026-6462 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting organisations through an open competitive process to apply to deliver community infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities program from 2026–27. The Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities grant opportunity provides total funding of up to $41.6 million (GST exclusive) for construction, upgrade or extension of infrastructure. You can apply for one of 3 streams of grant funding based on the type of infrastructure project and amount of grant funding you require for the project. The grant opportunity is comprised of 2 funding opportunities, called batches. You can apply for funding in one batch. Batch 1 opens on 7 April 2026 and closes on 18 May 2026. Batch 2 opens on 18 May 2026 and closes on 12 November 2026. The following groups and projects will be prioritised for funding: new and emerging multicultural communities, as defined below projects focussed on achieving positive outcomes for multicultural women, multicultural LGBTIQA+ community members, and multicultural people with a disability. Co-contributions are required towards the value of your project and the minimum amount of co funding is determined by whether you are applying as a priority group/project or other.

grants.title: GO8220: Saluting their Service Commemorative Grants Program 2026–27
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for all 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 9:00 PM AEST on 29 July 2026 - ID 2025-5415 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 9:00 PM AEDT 21 January 2027 - ID 2025-5416 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations to apply for grant funding under the Saluting Their Service Commemorative Grants Program (STS program). The objective of the STS Program is to commemorate the service and sacrifice of Australia’s service personnel who served in wars, conflicts and peace operations, including National Service personnel, and their families. The intended outcome of the STS Program is to provide funding for projects and activities that: promote appreciation and understanding of the experiences of service, and the role of service personnel preserve, add to the sum of knowledge on, or provide access to information about Australia’s wartime heritage. 1. Community Grants Grants up to $10,000 are available for projects and activities that: are focused on the local community commemorate the service and sacrifice of local community members are primarily accessed by the local community. 2. Major Grants Grants between $10,001 and $150,000 are available for major commemorative projects and activities that are significant from a national, state, territory and/or broader regional perspective. These projects may include the construction of new war or peace memorials where none currently exist, as well as additions to existing memorials. If your project relates to restoring or changing a memorial or other commemorative artefact, there may be heritage and conservation considerations.

grants.title: GO8607: Festivals Australia - Round 23
grants.summary: Festivals Australia provides funding to support individual art projects in regional or remote locations. Eligible projects take place at festivals, or significant one-off community events such as a town celebration or opening of a new community resource. Festivals Australia will: provide access to a diverse range of engaging, innovative arts projects that grow audiences at festivals across regional and remote Australia, support partnerships and collaboration across the arts sector, and encourage community participation in arts projects at regional and remote festivals. The program delivers two funding rounds each year usually opening in February and September. The Minister for the Arts (or their delegate) approves funding under the Program Guidelines. To check if your project is taking place in an eligible location, visit the Festivals Australia Eligibility Map. Enter the full address where your project will be delivered into the search box, or click on the location on the map. The remoteness classification, and whether this location is eligible, will be displayed.

grants.title: GO8640: Volunteer Grants 2025-26: Farrer
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations through a closed, non-competitive process to apply for a Volunteer Grant under the Families and Communities Program – Volunteer Grants Activity. The 2025–26 Volunteer Grants round began with a call for Expressions of Interest (EOI) by Federal Members of Parliament (MPs) who consulted with a community committee to develop a list of organisations to nominate. Following the EOI process, MPs nominated organisations to receive an invitation to apply. The nomination period for MPs to submit their nominations for the main 2025–26 Volunteer Grants round closed on 17 April 2026. This Volunteer Grants Activity is specific to the Farrer electorate only and is directly linked to the main Volunteer Grants Activity – 2025–26 Volunteer Grants round. Due to the resignation of the previous Federal MP for Farrer in February 2026, the 2025–26 Volunteer Grants process for this electorate was deferred until a new Federal MP was elected. The nomination period for the MP for Farrer closed on 14 September 2026. The Volunteer Grants Activity is an element of the Families and Communities Program, which recognises the valuable work of Australia’s volunteers. This initiative forms part of the Australian Government’s ongoing commitment to encourage, support and increase participation in volunteering. Eligible not-for-profit community organisations can use grant funding to cover expenses for online communication and insurance items, small equipment, training, and background screening checks for the main purpose of supporting the volunteer cohorts and volunteer-run activities specified in the 2025–26 Volunteer Grants – Farrer Grant Opportunity Guidelines. The intended outcome of the activity is to strengthen community functioning by supporting and increasing participation in volunteering.

grants.title: GO8589: Comprehensive Primary Health Care – New Entrants
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to provide funding for selected Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services (ACCHSs), currently delivering General Practitioner services, to provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) under the Indigenous Australians’ Health Programme (IAHP) who have not previously been funded to do so. This funding will be available over four years from 2026-27 to 2029-30. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: • provide First Nations people with improved access to culturally appropriate comprehensive primary health care services by: Supporting ACCHSs to expand or enhance service availability, service frequency, the range of services offered, workforce capability, service integration and geographic coverage • support ACCHSs to deliver culturally appropriate comprehensive primary health care services tailored to the health needs and priorities of their communities, and • support ACCHSs to embed Continuous Quality Improvement and best practice clinical and organisational governance into CPHC service delivery, supporting good health outcomes for clients and service sustainability. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: • First Nations people can access culturally appropriate CPHC services, where and when they need it • ACCHSs deliver culturally appropriate CPHC services that meet the health needs and priorities of their local communities, and • ACCHSs deliver best practice CPHC services to their local communities. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8579: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) - Place-Based Funding
grants.summary: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a lifelong condition caused by prenatal exposure to alcohol, characterised by a range of physical, cognitive, behavioural, and developmental difficulties that can impact individuals, families, and communities. The purpose of this grant opportunity is designed to strengthen the diagnosis and management of FASD across Australian communities. By providing targeted funding, the program will enhance local capacity for screening, diagnosis, and ongoing monitoring, while fostering greater community awareness of the dangers associated with alcohol consumption during pregnancy or when planning to conceive. This grant opportunity will be made available through two (2) streams. Stream 1: FASD Diagnostic Services Stream 2: Innovative Models of Care Applicants must nominate one primary stream that best aligns with the core purpose of the activities being proposed. Where activities could align to both streams, applicants should select the stream that reflects the main intent and outcomes of the proposal. Funding and reporting requirements will align to the nominated stream. Note: Please refer to the Webinar slides and recording of the Drug and Alcohol Program Webinar that was held on 15 September 2026. Please also see Frequently Asked Questions - Version 2 published on 30 September 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8266: 2026 NHMRC-GACD: Multisectoral Approaches
grants.summary: Together with other Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD) Associate Members, NHMRC is inviting investigators to submit applications for implementation research maximising collaboration and coordination with sectors and in settings beyond the healthcare system to tackle chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) (as defined by the World Bank) and/or underserved populations in high-income countries (HICs). For NHMRC funding support in HICs, research must focus on Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander communities. The objective of the 2026 NHMRC-GACD grant opportunity is to fund implementation research focused on strategies leveraging opportunities provided by settings and sectors beyond the health system in LMICs and/or for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander communities in Australia. While the focus is on settings outside of the healthcare system, collaboration with the relevant healthcare system(s) as part of the project is expected to facilitate effective design and knowledge mobilisation.

grants.title: GO8550: Our Marine Parks Grants – Round 5
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations in an open process to apply to deliver services under the Our Marine Parks Grants Program, nationally, from June 2027 to May 2030. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to promote actions that align with the management programs of Australian Marine Parks Management Plans to: support Traditional Owners to: document and maintain their traditional knowledge, cultural sites and values associated with Sea Country in and adjacent to Australian Marine Parks participate in the management of Sea Country in Australian Marine Parks and in adjacent waters enhance community capacity and participation in marine park management, including through improved understanding of social and environmental values protect marine parks from threats and pressures, to minimise damage, and to improve the resilience of marine parks support relevant industries to understand and engage in marine park management – commercial and recreational fishing and tourism for example improve awareness and understanding of Australian Marine Parks and their management arrangements support compliance by marine park users improve scientific knowledge through research and monitoring in line with: Australian Marine Parks Science Priorities and/or the demonstrated priorities of First Nations groups with a connection to Australian Marine Parks. Note: if your project includes a component in adjacent waters, ensure you tell us in your application how this component contributes to Australian Marine Park management.

grants.title: GO8616: ASEAN-Australia Centre 2026-27 Grants Program
grants.summary: For the 2026-27 grants opportunity, the ASEAN-Australia Centre welcomes applications aligned with its mission and four pillars across three streams: Economic engagement; Creative industry and cultural connections; and Asia capability. Economic engagement initiatives may support networking, information exchange, awareness-raising, business matching and Asia capability for Australian business, including First Nations businesses. Creative industry and cultural connections may support exchanges, residencies, capacity-building, professional development, collaboration, export pathways and market development. Asia capability initiatives may draw on Southeast Asian student expertise, establish professional benchmarking or accreditation, or develop Australian Curriculum-aligned teaching resources. Projects must involve multiple Southeast Asian countries and identify Southeast Asian partners. The intended outcome is to build business, cultural and community links between Southeast Asia and Australia.

grants.title: GO8592: African Australian Communities Program Stream 1 – Round 3
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations through a closed non-competitive process to apply to deliver services in New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia, under Program 2.5 Multicultural Affairs and Citizenship Program over 3 years from 2026-27 to 2028-29. The grant responds to the African Australian communities needs highlighted in the Multicultural Framework Review report, Towards Fairness: A Multicultural Australia for all. It will bolster assistance to African Australian communities to support their integration in the Australian community. The objective of the program is: to bolster the capacity of African-led and other organisations with demonstrated experience working with African Australians to further the settlement and integration journey of African Australian communities in Australia. The intended outcomes of the program are: to support African Australian communities to further their participation, integration and sense of belonging in Australia and enhance community cohesion. The invited applicants have demonstrated experience working with African Australian communities to deliver projects in one or more of the following key focus areas: youth programs that support African Australian youth to participate in Australian society or re-engage following experiences in the criminal justice mental health programs employment services and employment opportunities that are culturally appropriate and tailored to the specific needs of African Australians family programs such as, parenting support and support for survivors of domestic violence establishing projects to build capacity and capability in grassroots African Australian community organisations facilitating culturally appropriate access to Commonwealth services. This grant will be administered by the Community Grants Hub on behalf of the Department of Home Affairs. The grant is to be undertaken in accordance with the Commonwealth Grants Rules and Principles 2024.

grants.title: GO8621: Thriving Kids – First Nations Sector Strengthening
grants.summary: The aim of the grant opportunity is to deliver the Thriving Kids First Nations Sector Strengthening activity, as part of the Commonwealth’s commitment to provide dedicated First Nations national workforce activities from December 2026 until 30 June 2031. Funding will be provided for a 5-year period. This grant opportunity: focuses on uplifting the capability of National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation (NACCHO) member organisations and jurisdictional affiliates, acknowledges that Thriving Kids will be delivered and facilitated by and within various sectors, and will require collaboration across education, early childhood, health and community services. The purpose of the grant is to: Bring a First Nations voice and perspective to design, implementation and roll-out of Thriving Kids services, through established Thriving Kids governance arrangements, including informing the development and implementation of the Thriving Kids Workforce and Training Capability Framework Enable the community-controlled sector to build workforce capability skills to identify/screen and connect Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children with developmental delay and autism, and their families, carers and kin with Thriving Kids supports that match their developmental support needs. Overall, the grant activity will engage NACCHO to deliver the sector strengthening activity in a two-steam approach, including ongoing collaboration between the Commonwealth, NACCHO, cross sector peaks and states and territories, to ensure that national activities align with and inform local implementation and priorities. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8618: Children and Family Support
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations via a restricted process to apply to deliver services under Program 2.1 Families and Communities – Families and Children Activity - Children and Family Support (CaFS) program from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2032. The CaFS program aims to strengthen family wellbeing by delivering flexible, responsive supports for families with children aged 0–17 years, and young people up to age 25, where appropriate. The CaFS program aims to achieve the following 2 outcomes: Parents and caregivers receive the support they need to guide children’s social and emotional growth in families and communities that are safe and strong. Children and young people receive social and emotional support they need. Funding under the CaFS program will be targeted to the following 4 investment priorities: To invest early to improve family wellbeing, break cycles of disadvantage, and reduce the need for later interventions like child protection. Connected or integrated services that work together to meet family needs. Ensure services are informed by, and respond to, community needs. Improve outcomes for First Nations children and families by increasing the number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community-controlled organisations (ACCOs) delivering supports in locations with high First Nations populations.

grants.title: GO8604: Supporting Participation Program – 2026-27
grants.summary: The Supporting Participation Program (full title – Supporting Participation by Representatives of People with Disability in Key International Forums on Human Rights Program) provides funding for people with disability, through representative and advocacy organisations, to participate in key international disability and human rights forums. The program aims to ensure the voices and experiences of Australians with disability are represented in global discussions on disability rights, inclusion and policy development. Funding in 2027 will support participation at the: · United Nations (UN) 20th Session of the Conference of States Parties (COSP20) to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), New York, USA, 9 to 11 June 2027 · UN 71st Session of the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71), New York, USA, 8 to 19 March 2027; and · Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction (APMCDRR), Sendai, Japan, 25 to 29 October 2027. Delegates will contribute to international discussions on disability rights, build advocacy skills, expand professional networks, and strengthen the Australian disability sector's engagement in global forums. The program includes both General Delegates (aged over 18 years) and Emerging Young Leaders (aged 18 to 35 years), with an emphasis on leadership development, mentoring and capacity building. Delegates and organisations are expected to actively participate in forum activities, collaborate with stakeholders, meet all program requirements, support delegate wellbeing, manage risks, and share outcomes and learnings with the disability sector. Funding primarily supports in-person attendance, while allowing flexibility for virtual participation where required. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8600: Targeted Call for Research: Strengthening the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Workforce Pipeline 2026
grants.summary: A Targeted Call for Research (TCR) is a one-time request for grant applications designed to stimulate research in a particular area that will benefit the health of Australians or address a specific health issue. A strong, culturally safe and sustainable Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workforce is widely recognised as an enabler of health equity, building stronger community engagement while improving access to health services and developing sustainable culturally responsive models of care. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health professionals therefore play a vital role in improving trust in healthcare services, leading to better continuity of care that integrates community leadership and ultimately ensuring health systems are responsive to the needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. The objectives of TCR: Strengthening the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Workforce Pipeline to Improve Health Equity 2026 are: • To improve understanding of the enablers and barriers influencing attraction, education, recruitment, retention, career progression and leadership across Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workforce pipeline, including diverse and non-linear workforce pathways. • To evaluate the effectiveness, sustainability and cultural responsiveness of existing workforce development initiatives, models and strategies including contextual conditions that support their success. • To strengthen research and evaluation capability in the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workforce through meaningful participation, training and leadership opportunities. • To develop practical and culturally responsive tools, frameworks and measures to support workforce evaluation, planning and continuous improvement. • To generate evidence-based recommendations that support scalable, gender-balanced workforce development approaches and long-term improvements in health equity.

grants.title: GO8615: NHMRC Centres of Research Excellence 2027
grants.summary: The objectives of the CRE scheme are to improve health outcomes and promote or improve translation of research outcomes into policy and/or practice. The CRE scheme also supports researchers in capacity building activities, including in specific areas of need identified by NHMRC. The intended outcomes of the CRE scheme are to: • support the conduct and development of innovative, high quality, collaborative research • promote effective translation of research into knowledge gain, health policy and/or practice • foster and build capacity and capability in the health and medical research workforce • provide opportunities to expand and improve collaborations between research teams. The CRE 2027 grant opportunity will provide support for teams of researchers to purshue collaborative research and develop capacity in basic science research, clinical research, health services research and public health research. Applicants select the application stream that best fits their research proposal. Applicants should refer to the Centres of Research Excellence 2027 Guidelines for further guidance in selecting the appropriate stream. A CRE may be a single physical entity or institute, or a geographically disparate network linking across more than one institution. Centres are encouraged to collaborate with, and participate in, national and international research studies.

grants.title: GO8477: MRFF – PHCRI – 2026 Primary Health Care Research Grant Opportunity
grants.summary: The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) – Primary Health Care Research Initiative (PHCRI) aims to enable or support an increase in Australia’s evidence base in primary health care through research to improve service delivery and patient outcomes, and translate this knowledge into action. The objective of this grant opportunity is to provide grants of financial assistance to support medical research and medical innovation projects that: investigate and trial approaches, including adapting successful trials, to advance equity in primary health care services. are co-designed with primary health care services and consumers. Two streams of funding are available: Stream 1 (Targeted Call for Research): The organisation undertaking the majority of the research must be located in any area according to the Modified Monash Model (MM1-7). Stream 2 (Targeted Call for Research): The organisation undertaking the majority of the research is located in, and the Chief Investigator A and 50% or more of all Chief Investigators, and all research participants, are primarily resident in a regional, rural or remote area according to the Modified Monash Model (MM2-7). The intended outcome of the research is to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians by advancing equity in primary health care services. Applicants to this grant opportunity must propose to conduct research that delivers against the above objectives and those of the Primary Health Care Research Initiative. This grant opportunity is being administered by NHMRC on behalf of the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. Further information on the Medical Research Future Fund is available from the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing's website. A list of Eligible Organisations can be found on the NHMRC List of MRFF Eligible Organisations webpage.

grants.title: GO8649: LGBTIQA+ Health Program – Round 2
grants.summary: The LGBTIQA+ Health Program (LHP) is administered by LGBTIQ+ Health Australia on behalf of the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. The LHP contributes to delivery of the National Action Plan for the Health and Wellbeing of LGBTIQA+ People 2025–2035 (National Action Plan) in line with the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (PGPA Act) and the Commonwealth Grants Rules and Principles 2024 (CGRPs). Organisations with specialist expertise in LGBTIQA+ health and wellbeing are invited to apply for one-off competitive grants to support new and existing initiatives at the local, regional and national level that will foster access to appropriate, culturally sound and inclusive health care. The Australian Government has allocated a total of $11.9 million until the 2027-2028 financial year (inclusive) for the LHP. $8.1 million was committed to projects funded in the first round of the LHP. This is the final, planned substantive LHP grant round. LGBTIQ+ Health Australia (LHA) is the first point of contact for the LGBTIQA+ Health Program. All supporting documents related to this Grant Opportunity are available on the LHA website. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.
